India's PIN (Postal Index Number) code system was introduced on August 15, 1972 [d4][d5][d9]. The system was designed to streamline the sorting and delivery of mail by assigning a unique six-digit code to every post office, helping overcome challenges such as identical place names and letters written in multiple languages [d5][d2]. The initiative was conceived and implemented by Shriram Bhikaji Velankar, who was the additional secretary in the Union Ministry of Communications and a senior member of the Posts and Telegraphs Board [d4][d5][d6]. The date of introduction — August 15 — coincided with India's Independence Day, and specifically with the silver jubilee of India's independence in 1972 [d9][d1].
